finding.claim: decode(..., subject=X) accepts a validly signed token that has no sub claim, because _validate_sub returns early when sub is absent instead of raising MissingRequiredClaimError.
finding.source: Attacker holds a token signed by the same key that lacks a sub claim (another token type or service token from the same issuer).

trace.note: decode_complete calls _validate_claims with subject after signature verification
if 'sub' not in payload: return (bypasses subject check)
contrast: _validate_iss raises MissingRequiredClaimError when iss is absent

finding.guards_checked: Signature verification (passes, token is genuinely signed); verify_sub defaults True but early return skips comparison; require option is not set by default; workaround is options={'require':['sub']}.

finding.claim: get_signing_key_from_jwt triggers a synchronous, unthrottled JWKS refetch for any unknown or missing kid, with no negative cache or single-flight.
finding.source: Unauthenticated token whose unverified header carries a random or absent kid.
finding.sink: fetch_data outbound HTTP request to the JWKS endpoint, invoked via get_signing_keys(refresh=True).

trace.note: kid read from unverified header via decode_token(verify_signature=False)

finding.guards_checked: URI scheme restricted to http/https (line 90-95); redirects blocked by _NoRedirectHandler (17-27); timeout set. Missing: minimum refresh interval, negative caching, concurrency lock.

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, the per-kid lru_cache never time-expires, so a key removed from the JWKS (e.g. after compromise) remains trusted for its kid until LRU eviction at max 16 entries.
finding.source: Token signed with a key the issuer has since revoked, for a kid that was resolved earlier.
finding.sink: Cached PyJWK returned by get_signing_key without consulting the JWKS.

trace.note: get_signing_key cache hit short-circuits JWKS lookup

finding.guards_checked: Default cache_keys=False avoids the issue; cache is documented as no-expiry; eviction only by LRU size.

finding.claim: Unverified payload parse catches only ValueError, so an attacker-supplied deeply nested payload raises an uncaught RecursionError (not a PyJWTError) on the get_signing_key_from_jwt path.
finding.source: Unauthenticated token with a payload nested about 1000 levels deep.
finding.sink: json.loads of the payload in _decode_payload, executed before signature verification on the verify_signature=False path.

trace.note: header parse path does catch RecursionError, showing the payload path is inconsistent

finding.guards_checked: Signature check is bypassed by design on this path; header path has RecursionError handling; no size or depth limit on payload parse.
